title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer CB fallback ordering under regional failover
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer fallback ordering to prevent incorrect circuit-breaker fallbacks during concurrent regional failovers. No user-facing API changes. Recommended to promote to production immediately.
body:
Context: During a recent regional failover incident we observed the SLO-enforcer's circuit-breaker (CB) fallback logic choose suboptimal fallback targets when multiple regional failover and load-shedding events overlapped. Root cause: non-deterministic ordering and a race in route reassignment combined with stale in-memory candidate lists, which allowed a fallback decision to be applied out of order and caused cascading capacity pressure in the target region.

This PR stabilizes the CB fallback ordering and adds defensive checks to prevent out-of-order application of fallback decisions across concurrent failover events. It is a hotfix that should be merge-squashed and rolled out with the existing canary policy.

Summary of changes (single-string description required): Implement per-decision monotonic tokens to order fallback operations; convert fallback application to a compare-and-swap flow that verifies token monotonicity and route version; add a short-lived global retry backoff for simultaneous cross-region reassignments; protect candidate list construction with an RCU-style snapshot to avoid reading partially-updated routing tables; add unit and integration tests that reproduce the race; increase CB fallback hysteresis in the short term to reduce thrashing; update ops runbook to document the token and recovery steps.

Checklist:
- [x] Add ordering token and CAS application in enforcer
- [x] Snapshot routing table when building candidate lists
- [x] Unit + integration tests covering concurrent failover ordering
- [x] Canary rollout instructions and runbook update
- [x] Post-merge follow-up: remove temporary hysteresis bump after 2 weeks if stable

Motivation: Prevent incorrect fallback choices that can amplify cross-region pressure and lead to cascading SLO violations. The fix is intentionally conservative: it enforces ordering and shrinks the window for stale reads, while the hysteresis adjustment reduces oscillation risk during the next 24–72 hours of traffic.

Commits (high-level):
- 9fa3b2c hotfix: add monotonic fallback tokens and CAS apply flow
- 6e4d7b1 fix: snapshot routing table when building fallback candidates
- d2f1e88 test: add concurrent-failover integration test
- aabb334 perf: small refactor to minimize lock hold time in enforcer
- cc99ff2 docs: ops runbook update for fallback token diagnostics

Testing and CI: All unit tests and enforcer integration tests were run. Integration test initially flaked in CI due to simulator timing; re-run passed. Canary run in staging (traffic mirror) exercised the hotfix under synthetic failover bursts and showed stable behavior for 6 hours with no CB misfires.

Deployment and rollback plan: Squash-merge to main. Canary deploy to 5% of traffic for 30 minutes, then 25% for 1 hour, then full rollout. If suspicious regressions appear (increase in cross-region 5xx or CB firing > 2x baseline), rollback to previous release and escalate to oncall.

Related: ENG-482 (ordering regressions during failover), SRE-119 (incident postmortem), SUP-3321 (customer-reported failover thrash).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you explain how tokens are generated and whether they persist across restarts?

Maya Chen: Tokens are monotonic uint64s generated from an in-memory atomic counter; they are scoped to controller lifetime and not persisted - the CAS semantics only need monotonic ordering within a single control-plane leader. Will add note to runbook.
Lena Ortiz: Integration test is flaky locally for me, sometimes timing causes both paths to choose same candidate. Can we make the test deterministic by injecting a controllable clock?
Maya Chen: Good call - updated test to use a simulated clock and added a short jitter to the production path only. Reran CI and the test is stable.
Samir Rao (approval): Verified logic and tests. Observability hooks (token in traces/metrics) look good. Approving for merge with squash.
Arjun Patel: Please monitor CB firing and cross-region 5xx during canary. If anything looks off, revert.
conversation_summary: Post-incident hotfix that introduces ordering tokens and CAS semantics in the SLO enforcer fallback flow. Reviewed and approved after adding deterministic test scaffolding and addressing concerns about token lifetime and observability. Canary staged and then merged to main. Ops runbook updated for diagnostics and rollback guidance.
